name: ralph-loop
description: Ralph refinement loop with role-routed, cross-family model pairs. A seeder writes a behaviour-sliced review plan (an area is one promise traced from entry point to sink; a seam is one row reviewed in both directions) and a critic on another model family applies the merge test and the seam test before the loop starts. Phase 1 works single-system areas interleaved by risk: review 1 is the wiring lens (does the path exist and is it fed?), review 2 the failure lens (how does it fail?), each refined by one family and assessed by another. Phase 2 works the paired seam table. Seeded plans must fit their pass budget, test runs are scoped to the diff, every in-loop commit carries [skip ci] with exactly one CI run on the finished branch, and a run interrupted by a quota wall resumes on the same branch with every earned approval intact. Every pass then crosses a deterministic tamper gate; judgeable findings go to a judge on the family opposite the pass's doer, and a voided pass is reverted and scored as no progress.
author: arbitron

inputs.name: base_branch
inputs.description: THE BRANCH TO REFINE. The worktree is cut from it and the PR targets it, so refinement lands back on this branch rather than the repo default.

inputs.name: slug
inputs.description: Short kebab-case label for the work branch and doc naming. Empty derives a neutral placeholder.

inputs.name: force_fresh
inputs.description: Start a new body-of-work review even when base_branch carries an inherited Ralph plan. Creates a new refinement branch and runs existing archival, baseline capture, and plan seeding. False preserves automatic resume.

inputs.name: replan
inputs.description: On a RESUMED run only: re-plan the review before continuing. The cross-family critic (critique-replan) applies the merge test and the seam test to the plan the branch already carries, converting layer-sliced areas into behaviours and directional mirror rows into one row per seam, then the verifier and a checkpoint push run before the first new pass. Earned approvals are kept under the in-flight rule (a merged row keeps a tick only if every constituent had it; an unreviewed folded-in part needs another review path or the box reopens), and every decision is recorded under '## Plan critique' in RALPH.md. Ignored on a fresh run, which is critiqued anyway.

inputs.name: pr_base
inputs.description: Branch the final PR targets when it is not base_branch. A resumed run continues ON base_branch, so head and base are the same ref and push-and-pr can open no PR; name the feature's real base here (e.g. feat/age-filtering) so a resumed run still opens its PR. Empty keeps the previous behaviour (PR against base_branch, or none when resumed).

inputs.name: scope_note
inputs.description: Optional free text narrowing or annotating the review scope. The branch diff is always the primary signal; this only adds context.

inputs.name: max_ralph_iterations
inputs.description: Backstop cap on the ralph refinement loop. A seam-based plan of N single-system areas and P paired reviews needs 2N+P passes MINIMUM with zero rework (one observed plan: 26 areas + 112 pairs = 164), and most areas need several passes, so 200 left almost no headroom.

inputs.name: no_progress_streak
inputs.description: Consecutive passes with no forward progress, carried between passes. Read by the refine template; the loop's wedge exit is max_no_progress_streak.

inputs.name: max_no_progress_streak
inputs.description: Consecutive no-progress passes that count as a WEDGED loop rather than a hard review. This is the hard-wedge backstop, not a completion signal: the plan counter decides when the loop is DONE, and this decides only when it has stopped being able to make progress at all. It was an inlined 3, which ended run a1aab074 at pass 161 of a 500 cap with 98 approval boxes still unticked (3 of 52 single-system reviews, all 92 paired). That run was not wedged — a withheld approval is the NORMAL outcome of a review pass, and two of its three strikes were a refiner burning its hour waiting on a slow integration suite. 12 sits above record-pass-commit's sticky approval-stall limit of 8, so a real wedge still trips the stall flag first and then exits within a few more passes, while ordinary withholds no longer end a healthy run.

inputs.name: in_place
inputs.description: Refine base_branch itself instead of cutting a dev-* work branch, and open the PR into pr_base. Requires a pr_base that differs from base_branch, or no PR could be opened.

inputs.name: focus_seed
inputs.description: Worktree-relative path to a survivors file from a harden stage. When set, the seeder and the re-plan critic make every focus_items id a named area (the verifier fails the plan if one is missing) and the PR carries a harden-shortfall note. Empty means no seed.

inputs.name: baseline_path
inputs.description: Worktree-relative path to a committed branch-point test baseline. When set (and present at the tip of base_branch), the run imports it instead of measuring one with baseline-tests. Empty measures as before.

inputs.name: teams_webhook_url
inputs.description: Power Automate / Teams webhook for completion alerts. Empty makes the notify steps no-ops.

nodes.label: Init workspace
nodes.description: Clone repo_url at base_branch. force_fresh=true creates an isolated refinement branch even when a prior review plan exists; default preserves automatic resume.

nodes.label: Promote vars
nodes.description: Lift init-workspace outputs to top-level vars.

nodes.label: Notify: started
nodes.description: In-app notification that the loop has started.

nodes.label: Resuming?
nodes.description: Resume only when base_branch carries docs/reference/focus-areas.md AND force_fresh is false. Explicit fresh runs follow derive-scope, archival, baseline, and seeding; the resume path optionally re-plans (replan=true) before restoring counters, so a run seeded under older rules can be tightened without losing earned approvals.

nodes.label: Derive review scope
nodes.description: Fetch the default branch and compute what this branch changed vs its merge base. init-workspace shallow-clones ONLY the base ref, so origin/main is absent and this must fetch it before any merge-base is possible; falls back to a two-dot diff when the history is too shallow.

nodes.label: Archive prior ralph docs
nodes.description: Copy any existing RALPH.md, docs/reference/focus-areas.md and docs/reference/gaps-identified.md into docs/reference/historical/ with a dated, intra-day-numbered name before they are overwritten.

nodes.label: Import or measure baseline?
nodes.description: A run given baseline_path (confirmed present at the tip by init-workspace) imports that committed baseline instead of spending an agent pass measuring one. Otherwise baseline-tests measures it as before.

nodes.label: Import committed baseline
nodes.description: Validates the record-baseline shape of ./work/<baseline_path> and copies it to {{workspace}}/test-baseline.json, where record-baseline lifts it into variables exactly as it would a measured one. Fails the run on an unusable file: an explicitly named baseline that cannot be used is an input error.

nodes.label: Capture test baseline
nodes.description: Detect and run the project's test suite(s), writing {{workspace}}/test-baseline.json so the loop gates on NEW failures rather than a green suite.

nodes.label: Seed review plan
nodes.description: Writes RALPH.md (all three role protocols), the single-system plan (behaviour areas with entry, sink, files and a checklist per lens), the paired seam plan (one row per seam, SHARED/TRACE/BREAK) and gaps-identified.md, sized to fit the pass budget. Runs at high effort with the full context window: it runs once and its output sets the cost of every pass after it.

nodes.label: Critique review plan
nodes.description: Cross-family plan critic. Applies the merge test (areas are behaviours, not layers or files), the block test (entry, sink, files, a checklist per lens), the seam test (shared state, contract, flag or ordering; different authors; silent failure) and the budget to the seeded plan, merging and striking in place and recording every decision under '## Plan critique' in RALPH.md. The seeder's own slicing is the thing under review, so this runs on a different model family from the seeder. Fresh path only; a resumed run keeps its plan.

nodes.label: Verify ralph seed
nodes.description: Fails the run unless RALPH.md carries a Wrap Up, self-assessment and promise tags for EACH of the three roles; unless 2*singles + paired fits the pass budget (a paired row costs a whole pass: 96 rows took 66 passes); unless every paired row is one seam (no directional mirror rows) and checkbox syntax lives only in the two tables; and, when the critic ran, unless RALPH.md carries its '## Plan critique' record.

nodes.label: Checkpoint: push seed
nodes.description: Push the archived docs and the freshly seeded review plan before any refinement starts, so the planning work survives a later crash or cancel.

nodes.label: Re-plan first?
nodes.description: Resume path only. replan=true sends the resumed plan through the cross-family critic, the verifier and a checkpoint push BEFORE restore-state rebuilds the counters, so the counters reflect the tightened plan. Default continues straight to restore-state.

nodes.label: Critique plan in flight
nodes.description: Cross-family critic for a resumed run: rebuilds the single table as behaviours and the paired table as one row per seam, keeps every earned approval the in-flight rule allows (a merged row keeps a tick only if every constituent had it; an unreviewed folded-in part needs another review path or the box reopens), maps old area numbers to new ones for the gap ledger, and records everything under '## Plan critique'. Two runs seeded under the old rules had 54 and 131 passes ahead of them; the same work under the new shape is about 22 and 18.

nodes.label: Verify re-planned seed
nodes.description: Same verifier as the fresh path, run on the re-planned files: per-role protocol markers, 2*singles + paired within budget, one row per seam, boxes only in tables, and the critic's '## Plan critique' record (the script accepts critique-replan as the critic).

nodes.label: Checkpoint: push re-plan
nodes.description: Push the tightened plan before restore-state and the first new pass, so the re-plan survives a later crash or cancel.

nodes.label: Restore loop state
nodes.description: Resume path: restores the COMMITTED branch-point baseline and rebuilds the per-workspace counters from what the branch already carries. The plan is not re-seeded. Re-measuring the baseline on a partly-refined branch would record the previous run's own fixes as pre-existing and blind the regression gate.

nodes.label: Record baseline vars
nodes.description: Lift the baseline into test_baseline / test_commands / baseline_summary vars, and commit it as docs/reference/test-baseline.json (only when it changed) so checkpoint-push-baseline publishes it before the first pass-mark (R3).

nodes.label: Checkpoint: push baseline
nodes.description: Pushes the committed branch-point baseline before the first pass-mark (R3). Every tamper-gated range starts after this commit, so the baseline file can never read as baseline_edited, and a pass that does edit it is caught.

nodes.label: Select next work
nodes.description: The router. Picks the highest-risk outstanding item and emits next_kind, which decides BOTH what gets reviewed and which model pair handles it. Phase 1 works single-system areas (review 1 = the wiring lens, review 2 = the failure lens, each refined by one family and assessed by another); phase 2 begins only when every single box is ticked. Models are named only in the node profiles.

nodes.label: Mark pass start
nodes.description: Records HEAD at the start of this pass (the tamper gate's base) and a fresh pass_id nonce. pass_id, never the sha, is what ties a void to this pass: a reset-void returns HEAD to the same sha, so a sha cannot tell this pass's void from the last one's (P8).

nodes.label: Route by work kind
nodes.description: Every pair is cross-family on purpose: two passes by the same family share blind spots, which is the same opinion twice rather than redundancy. next_kind=none means nothing is outstanding and the loop exits.

nodes.label: Refine Single 1
nodes.description: Review 1 refiner: the WIRING lens (does the path exist and is it fed?). The approver runs on another model family.

nodes.label: Verify tests (single1)
nodes.description: Runs only the suites the pass's diff touched; skips entirely on an inspection-only pass; full sweep every 10th pass or on an unmapped path.

nodes.label: Assess Single 1
nodes.description: Review 1 approver, opposite family to the refiner. Ticks the Review 1 box when every wiring-lens check in the area block is demonstrated.

nodes.label: Refine Single 2
nodes.description: Review 2 refiner: the FAILURE lens (how does it fail?), on a different family from review 1 and asking a different question.

nodes.label: Verify tests (single2)
nodes.description: Runs only the suites the pass's diff touched; skips entirely on an inspection-only pass; full sweep every 10th pass or on an unmapped path.

nodes.label: Assess Single 2
nodes.description: Review 2 approver, opposite family to the refiner. Ticks the Review 2 box when every failure-lens check in the area block is demonstrated.

nodes.label: Refine Paired
nodes.description: Paired refiner: one seam per pass, both directions, BREAK shown impossible or caught; batches further rows only when they share loaded context.

nodes.label: Verify tests (paired)
nodes.description: Runs only the suites the pass's diff touched; skips entirely on an inspection-only pass; full sweep every 10th pass or on an unmapped path.

nodes.label: Assess Paired
nodes.description: Paired approver, opposite family to the refiner. Ticks a row when both directions hold and its BREAK is demonstrated; up to four rows, each cited separately.

nodes.label: Tamper gate
nodes.description: Deterministic check of the whole pass (refine plus assess commits) for weakened tests: deleted or renamed tests, dropped assertions, added skip/focus markers, test/mutation/CI config edits, baseline edits, and history rewritten inside the pass. Writes {{workspace}}/tamper/findings.json. Exit 2 means bad inputs only.

nodes.label: Void, judge or pass?
nodes.description: First-match, so the deterministic void comes first (R4): force_void (history rewritten inside the pass; ralph does not pass --tests-only, so source_changed never fires) cannot be judged because the diff is meaningless, and must win even when judgeable findings also exist. Judgeable findings go to a cross-family judge. A clean pass goes straight to record-pass-commit.

nodes.label: Void pass (forced)
nodes.description: Forced void without a judge: resets the worktree to the pass base, restores the tracking tables so no box ticked this pass survives, and records the must-fix items in gaps-identified.md. record-pass-commit then scores the pass as no progress.

operations.value: ralph pass {{ralph_iteration}}: {{select-work.next_kind}} on {{select-work.target_id}} ({{select-work.target_label}}); tracking in ./work/RALPH.md and ./work/docs/reference/

nodes.label: Judge context
nodes.description: Tells the judge what this pass was supposed to do, so it can rule each finding against the plan rather than against the diff alone.

nodes.label: Pick cross-family judge
nodes.description: The judge is the opposite family to the pass's doer (Q7). Doers: refine-single-1 is Sonnet (Claude), refine-single-2 is coder-codex-high (GPT), refine-paired is Opus (Claude). So only single_2 gets the Opus judge; everything else gets codex.

nodes.label: Tamper judge (codex)
nodes.description: GPT-family judge for passes done by a Claude doer (single_1, paired). Rules on every finding id and writes only {{workspace}}/tamper/verdict.json.

nodes.label: Tamper judge (opus)
nodes.description: Claude-family judge for passes done by the GPT doer (single_2). Rules on every finding id and writes only {{workspace}}/tamper/verdict.json.

nodes.label: Apply tamper verdict
nodes.description: Applies the judge's verdict, failing closed: a missing or malformed verdict, an unruled finding, or any legitimate:false voids the pass by restoring the weakened test/config/CI/baseline files and the tracking tables, appending must-fix items to gaps-identified.md and writing {{workspace}}/tamper/must-fix.md for the next pass. A pass that stands is left as is.

nodes.label: Record pass commit
nodes.description: Reads what the refinement pass actually committed (new commits since the previous pass, whether focus-areas.md / gaps-identified.md were touched) and emits progress_evidence. The assessor is toolless and used to score progress from {{refine.response}} alone — but the pass's Wrap Up asks it what REMAINS, so a compliant report structurally omits what it accomplished and the verdict became a coin flip that tripped the stagnation backstop on healthy runs. A commit is not a narrative. Never fails the run: no git evidence emits a conservative false and the assessor falls back to the pass's Progress: line.

nodes.label: Checkpoint: push pass
nodes.description: Pushes the pass once the tamper gate has ruled, including tamper-verdict's revert commit. The doers and approvers commit only, so a run that dies mid-pass never leaves an ungated pass on the branch. Agent commits carry [skip ci]; push-and-pr makes the one CI commit.

nodes.label: Count review plan
nodes.description: Counts outstanding approval boxes in focus-areas.md and emits plan_complete, so loop termination is arithmetic rather than narrative. refine-assess is toolless: it could only read the pass's own <promise>FINIT</promise> claim and had no way to contradict it. Run ae3ec85f exited that way at pass 56 of a 200 cap with all 112 paired integration reviews untouched — 114 of 164 approvals outstanding — and shipped a PR whose review plan was 70% unexecuted. Fails closed: an unreadable plan emits plan_complete=false, and the stagnation backstop plus the cap still bound the run.

nodes.label: Assess refinement
nodes.description: Read the pass's promise tag as strong evidence, then judge done against the review tables and the branch-point baseline.

nodes.label: Loop or exit
nodes.description: Exits on the pass budget, on an ARITHMETICALLY complete review plan, or on a wedge. The order is the point. count-review-plan exists to make termination arithmetic rather than narrative, but this gate used to read only ralph_iteration and refine-assess.consecutive_no_progress — the counter informed the toolless assessor and nothing else, so the guard could not reach the path it guarded. Run a1aab074 exited here at pass 161 of 500 on a bare 3-strike stagnation rule while count-review-plan.plan_complete was false and unchecked_boxes was 98, then opened a PR presenting that as a finished review. A withheld approval is the normal outcome of a review pass, so three in a row is not a wedged loop. plan_complete is now a first-class exit and the stagnation exit is the declared hard-wedge threshold (max_no_progress_streak, 12), which sits above record-pass-commit's sticky approval-stall limit of 8 so a genuine wedge is still caught within a few passes of stalling. Otherwise loops back to the ROUTER, not to a fixed refiner, so the next pass is re-routed by what the plan now needs. A quota failure is NOT handled here: the agent node fails the run, which is cleanly resumable.

nodes.label: Push & open PR
nodes.description: Push the work branch and open a PR targeting base_branch, so refinement lands back on the branch being refined.

nodes.label: Notify: PR opened
nodes.description: In-app notification that the loop finished. Carries the COUNTED plan state, not just the PR link: a run that exits on the wedge backstop with approval boxes outstanding must say so where someone will see it.

args: The refinement loop finished and opened a PR ({{push-and-pr.pr_url}}) against {{base_branch}}. {{count-review-plan.summary}}

nodes.label: Notify Teams
nodes.description: Rich completion alert (no-op when teams_webhook_url is unset).

nodes.label: Done (terminal)
nodes.description: Terminal node.
